new_note: *Pray ye therefore Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.* (Matthew 9:38) *Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers Perturbation of spirit and stupor of heart.* (2 Baruch 70:2) Yahusha (Jesus) sees the crowds and tells his disciples to ask Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest for labourers, because the harvest is standing ready. Baruch had already been told what that harvest is: the time of the age ripens, and what was sown in it, evil seed and good seed alike, has come up. The one Baruch calls the Mighty One is the owner of that field, so the prayer in Matthew is a prayer prayed inside that ripening time, and the next chapter sends the twelve out as the answer.
member_note: 2 Baruch 70:2 — *the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come.* The prayer Yahusha (Jesus) teaches in Matthew 9:38 asks for workers for this same harvest.
flag: Old note cited this verse as 2 Baruch 35:1 (stale numbering) and its quote trailed off; card is already on 70:2, citation fixed. Old note's word 'them' differs from live 'the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers'; quoted live text.

new_note: *For that time is the consummation of that which is corruptible, And the beginning of that which is not corruptible. Therefore those things which were predicted shall belong to it: Therefore it is far away from evils, and near to those things which die not.* (2 Baruch 74:2–3) *And Elohim (God) shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.* (Revelation 21:4) John sees the same turning in Revelation. When the corruptible reaches its end the incorruptible begins, and Baruch says that age is far from evils and near to those things which die not, which is what John means when there is no more death. Elohim (God) wipes the tears away because the former things have passed, and both writers are looking at the same line between this age and the one that does not end.
member_note: 2 Baruch 74:2 — *the consummation of that which is corruptible, And the beginning of that which is not corruptible.* John sees the same passing in Revelation 21:4, where there is no more death because the former things are passed away.
flag: Old note leaned on 'near to those things which die not' (2 Baruch 74:3), so I quoted 74:2 and 74:3 together and cited 74:2–3; no move needed.

new_note: *But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.* (Matthew 9:36) *And truly I know that behold all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.* (2 Baruch 78:3) Yahusha (Jesus) looks at the multitudes and finds them scattered and without a shepherd, which is a picture of a people and not of a crowd of strangers. Baruch writes to the brethren in captivity and says who that people is: the twelve tribes, bound by one bond because they are born from one father. However far they have been carried, they are one flock by birth, and that is what moves Yahusha (Jesus) to compassion.
member_note: 2 Baruch 78:3 — *all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.* The scattered, shepherdless multitudes Yahusha (Jesus) sees in Matthew 9:36 are this one family born from one father.
flag: Old note cited 2 Baruch 38:4 (stale numbering); fixed to the live 78:3.

new_note: *But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.* (Matthew 9:36) *For if ye so do these things, He will continually remember you, He who always promised on our behalf to those who were more excellent than we, that He will never forget or forsake us, but with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed.* (2 Baruch 78:7) Yahusha (Jesus) is moved with compassion at sheep scattered abroad with no shepherd. Baruch closes his letter to the scattered tribes with the promise that answers it: Yahuah (Lord) will never forget or forsake them, and with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed. The compassion in Matthew and the mercy in Baruch are one mercy, and its work is the gathering.
member_note: 2 Baruch 78:7 — *with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed.* The compassion Yahusha (Jesus) shows the scattered sheep in Matthew 9:36 is this promised mercy at work.
flag: Old note cited 2 Baruch 38:7 (stale numbering) and tied it to Hosea 6:6 at Matthew 9:13; I dropped the Hosea link because no live text for it was given to quote. Citation fixed to 78:7.

new_note: *And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;* (Matthew 27:51) *And therefore there have been given to thee counsel and understanding, That thou mightest instruct thy sons concerning this;* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 20:5) The verse before this one promises Levi a blessing for his seed until Yahuah (Lord) visits in tender mercies, and here he is given understanding so that he can teach his sons about that visit. The veil of the temple torn from the top to the bottom, in the house his sons served, is a plain sign that the way to the Father was opened from above and not forced from below.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 20:5 — *given to thee counsel and understanding, That thou mightest instruct thy sons concerning this.* Levi is given understanding to teach his sons about the visit of Yahuah (Lord), and the veil torn in Matthew 27:51 is a sign of it.
flag: WEAK FIT. The old note was written about Levi's vision of the gates of heaven opened and the holy temple (Testaments 21:1), which is not the neighbour of 20:5 (it is the neighbour of 21:2, card 4871), so I could not move this card there. I wrote a modest note on 20:5 and the torn veil; the author may want this card re-seated on 21:1.

new_note: *And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;* (Matthew 27:51) *And He said to me: Levi, I have given thee the blessings of the priesthood until I come and sojourn in the midst of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 21:2) Levi is told that the blessings of the priesthood are his until Yahuah (Lord) comes and sojourns in the midst of Yashar'el (Israel). Matthew shows what the end of that until looks like: when Yahusha (Jesus) has come and given his life, the veil of the temple is torn from the top to the bottom, and the way into the holy place stands open. Nothing of Torah is thrown out in this; the way to the Father is opened from above by the one who came to sojourn among his people.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 21:2 — *I have given thee the blessings of the priesthood until I come and sojourn in the midst of Yashar'el (Israel).* The until in Levi's blessing is met when the veil is torn in Matthew 27:51 and the one who sojourns has come.
flag: Old note also quoted the end of the verse before (Testaments 21:1, gates of heaven opened and the throne seen); I quoted 21:2 only since the point rests on the 'until I come and sojourn'.

new_note: *And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,* (Matthew 27:52) *And some of them shall be high priests, and judges, and scribes; For by their mouth shall the holy place be guarded.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 24:17) Levi is told that some of his seed will be high priests, judges and scribes, and that the holy place will be guarded by what they say. Matthew shows the saints who slept rising out of opened graves when Yahusha (Jesus) dies, which can be read as a foretaste of the resurrection of the faithful that is still ahead. The two meet on the same ground: the holy place and the faithful who served Yahuah (God) in it are not left to the grave.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 24:17 — *For by their mouth shall the holy place be guarded.* The faithful dead who rise in Matthew 27:52 are the same covenant line Levi's vision speaks of.
flag: LOOSE FIT. The old note's link (saints arising as a foretaste of the first resurrection) is kept but hedged as a reading; the connection to 'holy place guarded by their mouth' is thin and the author may wish to review or unseat it.

new_note: *Then saith Yahusha (Jesus) unto them, All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad.* (Matthew 26:31) *And behold, I am clear from your ungodliness and transgression, which ye shall commit in the end of the ages [against the Saviour of the world, Messiah (Christ), acting godlessly], deceiving Yashar'el (Israel), and stirring up against it great evils from Yahuah (Lord).* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 26:2) On the night of his arrest Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples they will all be offended because of him, and says it is written that the shepherd will be smitten and the sheep scattered. Long before, Levi told his sons that at the end of the ages they would act ungodly against the Saviour of the world, deceiving Yashar'el (Israel) and leaving it open to great evils. Both describe leadership failing and the flock scattered as a result. The one who is smitten was himself born of Yahudah (Judah) and came for his people, so what is named here is a corrupt leadership, not the people.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 26:2 — *I am clear from your ungodliness and transgression, which ye shall commit in the end of the ages.* Levi's warning of ungodly leaders at the end of the ages stands behind the smitten shepherd and scattered flock of Matthew 26:31.
flag: Old note cited this as Testament of Levi 17:2 (stale numbering); fixed to 26:2. The live verse carries square brackets around 'against the Saviour of the world, Messiah (Christ), acting godlessly' (a probable later insertion marked by the translator); I quoted them exactly and did not lean on the bracketed words. Old note's references to an internal framework were dropped, system-not-people kept.

new_note: *But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.* (Matthew 23:13) *And ye shall deal lawlessly together with Yashar'el (Israel), so He shall not bear with Jerusalem because of your wickedness; but the veil of the temple shall be rent, so as not to cover your shame.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 26:3) Yahusha (Jesus) charges the scribes and Pharisees with shutting up the kingdom of heaven against men, going in neither themselves nor letting others enter. Levi foresaw leaders of his own line dealing lawlessly with Yashar'el (Israel), and the veil of the temple being rent so that it would no longer cover their shame. In both the failing is a leadership that holds the door and breaks the commandments, and the people kept out are its victims. The veil of the temple is torn in Matthew 27:51, and the lawlessness of the keepers is laid bare.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 26:3 — *ye shall deal lawlessly together with Yashar'el (Israel), so He shall not bear with Jerusalem because of your wickedness.* Levi's lawless leaders who hold the door are the ones Yahusha (Jesus) faces in the first woe of Matthew 23:13.
flag: Old note cited Levi by a file chapter and the canonical chapter (stale); fixed to 26:3. I did not quote Matthew 27:51 because its live text was not in the packet.

new_note: *Then the high priest rent his clothes, saying, He hath spoken blasphemy; what further need have we of witnesses? behold, now ye have heard his blasphemy.* (Matthew 26:65) *And ye shall deal lawlessly together with Yashar'el (Israel), so He shall not bear with Jerusalem because of your wickedness; but the veil of the temple shall be rent, so as not to cover your shame.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 26:3) The high priest tears his own clothes and calls the truth blasphemy, though Torah forbids a high priest to rend his clothes (Leviticus 21:10). Levi had said that when the lawlessness of the leaders of his line was full, it would be the veil of the temple that was rent, so as not to cover their shame. One rending is a man's, done in anger to silence a witness; the other is Yahuah's (God), and it uncovers. The charge is against the office as it was being used, not against the people under it.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 26:3 — *the veil of the temple shall be rent, so as not to cover your shame.* The high priest rends his clothes in Matthew 26:65, and the veil that Levi said would be rent is torn soon after.
flag: Old note cited Levi 17:3 (stale); fixed to 26:3. Old note also tied Leviticus 10:6 and 21:10 and Hebrews 4:14–16 and 10:19–22; I mentioned Leviticus 21:10 in a clause but could not quote it (live text not in packet), and dropped the Hebrews links for the same reason. Please confirm Leviticus 21:10 as the right anchor.

new_note: *Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.* (Matthew 19:21) *Work righteousness, therefore, my children, upon the earth, That ye may have (it) as a treasure in heaven.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 29:5) Yahusha (Jesus) tells the rich young man that if he wants to be perfect he should go, sell what he has, give to the poor, and have treasure in heaven, and then come and follow. Levi tells his sons the same thing in other words: work righteousness on the earth, and it is kept as a treasure in heaven. Just before this, Yahusha (Jesus) had told the man that the way into life is to keep the commandments, so the treasure in heaven is what righteousness done on the earth is laid up as.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 29:5 — *Work righteousness, therefore, my children, upon the earth, That ye may have (it) as a treasure in heaven.* Levi's call to work righteousness on the earth and have it as a treasure in heaven is the word Yahusha (Jesus) speaks in Matthew 19:21.
flag: Old note cited this as Levi 7 verse 5 / chapter 18 (stale); fixed to 29:5. Also tied to 1 Timothy 6:18–19; dropped since no live text was given to quote.

new_note: *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.* (Matthew 23:15) *And in the seventh week shall come priests, (who are) idolaters, adulterers, lovers of money, proud, lawless, lascivious, abusers of children and beasts.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 33:11) Yahusha (Jesus) says the scribes and Pharisees cross sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made they make him twofold more the child of hell than themselves. Levi's vision of the weeks names the priests who come in the seventh week as idolaters, lovers of money, proud and lawless. A convert made by leaders like that is made into what they are, which is why the measure is whether a teacher keeps the commandments. The fault is in the system that made the proselyte, and the one it made is its victim.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 33:11 — *in the seventh week shall come priests, (who are) idolaters, adulterers, lovers of money, proud, lawless.* Levi's seventh-week priests, lawless and proud, are the kind of leaders Yahusha (Jesus) charges in Matthew 23:15.
flag: Old note cited Levi 'ch 20 / Testament of Levi 17' (stale); fixed to 33:11. Dropped the 'five costumes' passage and 1 John 2:3–4 aside as not belonging on this card and not quotable from the packet.

new_note: *And, behold, two blind men sitting by the way side, when they heard that Yahusha (Jesus) passed by, cried out, saying, Have mercy on us, O Adonai (Lord), thou Son of David.* (Matthew 20:30) *Until Yahuah (Lord) visit you, when with perfect heart ye repent and walk in all His commandments, and He bring you up from captivity among the Gentiles.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 58:5) Two blind men sit by the road and cry out for mercy to the Son of David as Yahusha (Jesus) passes. Yahudah (Judah) tells his sons of the hope that mercy is bound up with: Yahuah (Lord) will visit them when they repent with a perfect heart and walk in all his commandments, and will bring them up from captivity among the Gentiles. The Gentiles here are the nations where the seed was scattered, so the mercy these men ask for is the first of the homecoming that leads back to the commandments, not away from them.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 58:5 — *walk in all His commandments, and He bring you up from captivity among the Gentiles.* Yahudah (Judah) promises that Yahuah (Lord) will bring the repentant home from among the Gentiles, and the two men in Matthew 20:30 cry for that mercy.
flag: WRONG VERSE. The old note describes Testaments 37:5 (the star arising from Jacob), which is not the neighbour of 58:5 and so could not be moved. I wrote a modest note on 58:5 (visitation, return to the commandments, bring up from captivity) with Matthew 20:30; the card probably belongs on the star verse and the author may want it re-seated.

new_note: *And, behold, two blind men sitting by the way side, when they heard that Yahusha (Jesus) passed by, cried out, saying, Have mercy on us, O Adonai (Lord), thou Son of David.* (Matthew 20:30) *[This Branch of Elohim (God) El Elyon (Most High), And this Fountain giving life unto all.]* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:4) The two blind men call Yahusha (Jesus) the Son of David. The verse before this one has Yahudah (Judah) saying his sons will be sons in truth and will walk in His commandments first and last, and then he names the Branch of Elohim (God) that comes from his line and the Fountain giving life to all. The Son of David the blind men name is that Branch, and men who cannot see are the ones who know him by hearing his voice as he passes.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:4 — *This Branch of Elohim (God) El Elyon (Most High), And this Fountain giving life unto all.* The Branch from Yahudah's (Judah's) line is the Son of David the two blind men call out to in Matthew 20:30.
flag: Old note cited 38:4 (stale); fixed to 59:4. The live verse is wholly in square brackets; I quoted it exactly with the brackets. Old note's Jeremiah 23:5–6, Zechariah 6:12, Isaiah 11:1 and Ezekiel 34 links dropped because no live text was provided to quote.

new_note: *And the multitude rebuked them, because they should hold their peace: but they cried the more, saying, Have mercy on us, O Adonai (Lord), thou Son of David.* (Matthew 20:31) *Then shall the sceptre of my kingdom shine forth; And from your root shall arise a stem;* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:5) The multitude tells the blind men to hold their peace, and they cry out all the more, Son of David. Yahudah (Judah) says the sceptre of his kingdom will shine forth and a stem will rise from the root of his sons. The two men have no sight, yet they name the stem from the root of Yahudah (Judah) while the crowd, which can see, tries to silence them. They show what Yahusha (Jesus) said of his own sheep, that they hear his voice.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:5 — *the sceptre of my kingdom shine forth; And from your root shall arise a stem.* Two blind men keep crying Son of David against the crowd in Matthew 20:31, naming the stem Yahudah (Judah) was told would rise.
flag: Old note cited 38:5 (stale); fixed to 59:5. Dropped the cross-references to Matthew 9:27–31, 15:22 and 21:9, which could not be quoted from the packet.

new_note: *Tell ye the daughter of Sion, Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass, and a colt the foal of an ass.* (Matthew 21:5) *Then shall the sceptre of my kingdom shine forth; And from your root shall arise a stem;* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:5) Matthew shows the King coming to the daughter of Zion, meek and sitting on an ass, as the prophet had said. Yahudah (Judah) told his sons that the sceptre of his kingdom would shine forth and a stem rise from their root. The sceptre promised to the tribe of Yahudah (Judah) arrives not in a chariot but on a colt, and the daughter of Zion is told to look.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:5 — *the sceptre of my kingdom shine forth; And from your root shall arise a stem.* The sceptre promised to Yahudah (Judah) comes as the meek King on a colt in Matthew 21:5.
flag: Old note cited Judah ch 15 / 38 (stale); fixed to 59:5. Dropped Zechariah 9:9 and Isaiah 11:1 as separate quotes (no live text to quote).

new_note: *Tell ye the daughter of Sion, Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass, and a colt the foal of an ass.* (Matthew 21:5) *And from it shall grow a rod of righteousness to the Gentiles, To judge and to save all that call upon Yahuah (Lord).* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:6) Matthew shows the King coming to the daughter of Zion, meek, on a colt. Yahudah (Judah) says a rod of righteousness will grow from the stem that comes from his root, to judge and to save all who call upon Yahuah (Lord). The Gentiles here are best read as the scattered seed of Yashar'el (Israel) living among the nations, the ones the King is coming to gather and who call out to him, as the crowds of the entry will do. This is not a new people set in the place of the twelve tribes.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:6 — *a rod of righteousness to the Gentiles, To judge and to save all that call upon Yahuah (Lord).* Yahudah's (Judah's) rod of righteousness for the Gentiles points to the King coming in Matthew 21:5, whose call goes to the scattered seed.
flag: Old note cited Judah ch 15 v.6 (stale); fixed to 59:6. I hedged 'Gentiles' as 'best read as the scattered seed' because the verse itself does not say so; please confirm this reading.

new_note: *And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?* (Matthew 24:3) *For in the fortieth year of my life, I saw a vision on the Mount of Olives, on the east of Jerusalem, that the sun and the moon were standing still.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 90:1) The disciples sit on the mount of Olives and ask Yahusha (Jesus) the sign of his coming and of the end of the world. Naphtali, in the fortieth year of his life, saw a vision on that same mountain, east of Jerusalem. It is a place where what is coming is shown and asked about, and the two come together there.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 90:1 — *I saw a vision on the Mount of Olives, on the east of Jerusalem.* Naphtali saw his vision on the same Mount of Olives where the disciples ask about the end in Matthew 24:3.
flag: Old note cited Naphtali 4:1 (stale); fixed to 90:1. Dropped the Ezekiel 11:22–23 and Zechariah 14:4 links because no live text was given to quote. The note stays at the shared mountain; the vision's content (sun and moon, Isaac) is in the next verse and was not drawn in.

new_note: *And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.* (Matthew 24:14) *For through their tribes shall Elohim (God) appear [dwelling among men] on earth, To save the race of Yashar'el (Israel), And to gather together the righteous from amongst the Gentiles.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 93:3) Yahusha (Jesus) says the gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a witness to all nations, and then the end comes. Naphtali's last words say what the news is: Elohim (God) appears through the tribes to save the race of Yashar'el (Israel) and to gather the righteous from among the Gentiles. The Gentiles here are best read as the scattered seed of the twelve tribes living among the nations, which is why the news goes out broadly: the sheep are scattered everywhere, are not known by sight, and hear when they are called.
member_note: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 93:3 — *To save the race of Yashar'el (Israel), And to gather together the righteous from amongst the Gentiles.* The gospel preached to all nations in Matthew 24:14 is the news that the scattered are being gathered.
flag: Old note cited Naphtali 6:3 (stale); fixed to 93:3. I hedged 'Gentiles' as 'best read as the scattered seed'; Hosea 1:10 and Romans 9:25–26 dropped for want of live text to quote. The live verse carries the bracketed words [dwelling among men]; quoted exactly.
